newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lai Sun Hotels in HK$2.6 bln restructure.
newsitem.headline: Lai Sun Hotels in HK$2.6 bln restructure.

text.p: Lai Sun Hotels International Ltd said on Thursday it would buy stakes in three hotels and part of a property project in Shanghai from its parent Lai Sun Development Co Ltd for about HK$2.6 billion.

Lai Sun Hotels said in a statement it would pay for the purchase through the issue of 840.40 million new shares at HK$2.025 each, HK$401.19 million in cash and the issue of 215 million warrants giving Lai Sun Development the right to subscribe to up to HK$473 million worth of new shares.

Lai Sun Development said it intended to rationalise its holding structure "which is in line with the management's ongoing objective to unlock the intrinsic value of certain of its non-core assets through restructurings and spin-offs at the appropriate time".

The hotel purchases involve a 65 percent stake in The Ritz Carlton in Hong Kong, a 50 percent stake in the Four Seasons Hotel in New York, a 25 percent stake in the Regent Beverely Wilshire Hotel in Los Angeles and a 9.9 percent stake in a company holding the liquor licences necessary for the operation of the food and beverage premises at the Beverely Wilshire.
Lai Sun Hotels said it would buy the hotel assets for a total of HK$2.10 billion, representing a 12.6 percent discount to current market value.
It said it would also buy 181 serviced apartment units in the Hong Kong Plaza, a project under development in Shanghai, China, from its parent for HK$480 million.
Lai Sun Hotels said it was planning a new share placement to raise capital for the purchases and also repay debt.
Details of the new issue, which would be placed with institutional and professional investors, had yet to be fixed, it said.
Lai Sun Development currently owns about 54.09 percent of Lai Sun Hotels.

After exercising its warrants -- each of which which entitles Lai Sun Development to subscribe for one Lai Sun Hotels share at HK$2.20 each -- and after the proposed placement, the parent's stake will be reduced to 48 percent.
Lai Sun Development is 38.86 percent owned by Lai Sun Garment (International) Ltd.
The company said it would use the cash proceeds received from the restructuring to replenish its Hong Kong land bank and for general working purposes.
Lai Sun Hotels said it intends to continue expanding its core business of hotel ownership and management.
